class Account::DataTransfer::UserRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: User)
  end

  private
    def records
      User.where(account: account).includes(:identity)
    end

    def serialize_record(record)
      super.merge("email_address" => record.identity&.email_address)
    end

    def import_records(context)
      paths = zip.glob("#{model_dir}/*.json")
      raise Account::DataTransfer::ImportError, "This archive does not appear to be a Fizzy account export (missing user data)." if paths.empty?

      seen_identity_ids = Set.new

      paths.each do |path|
        rows = parse_json_array(path)
        next if rows.empty?

        mapped_rows = rows.map do |row|
          new_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
          context.id_map[model.name][row["id"]] = new_id

          identity = find_or_create_identity(row)
          if identity && !seen_identity_ids.add?(identity.id)
            identity = nil
          end

          attrs = import_attributes(row, context, new_id)
          attrs["identity_id"] = identity&.id
          attrs
        end

        User.insert_all!(mapped_rows)
      end

      ensure_importing_identity_has_user(context)
    end

    def find_or_create_identity(row)
      return nil if row["email_address"].blank? || row["active"] == false

      email = row["email_address"].to_s.strip.downcase
      Identity.find_by(email_address: email) || Identity.create!(email_address: email)
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
      Identity.find_by!(email_address: email)
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e
      raise Account::DataTransfer::ImportError, "Invalid user email address #{row["email_address"].inspect}: #{e.message}"
    end

    def ensure_importing_identity_has_user(context)
      identity = context.importing_identity
      return if context.new_account.users.active.exists?(identity_id: identity.id)

      name = identity.users.first&.name || identity.email_address.split("@").first
      user_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
      now = Time.current
      User.insert_all!([ {
        "id" => user_id,
        "account_id" => context.new_account.id,
        "identity_id" => identity.id,
        "name" => name,
        "role" => "owner",
        "active" => true,
        "verified_at" => now,
        "created_at" => now,
        "updated_at" => now
      } ])
      context.id_map["__importing_user_created__"] = user_id
    end
end
EOF

class Account::DataTransfer::FilterRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: ::Filter)
  end

  private
    def records
      ::Filter.where(account: account).includes(:boards, :tags, :assignees, :creators, :closers)
    end

    def serialize_record(record)
      super.merge(
        "board_ids" => record.association(:boards).target.map(&:id),
        "tag_ids" => record.tag_ids,
        "assignee_ids" => record.assignee_ids,
        "creator_ids" => record.creator_ids,
        "closer_ids" => record.closer_ids
      )
    end

    def import_records(context)
      zip.glob("#{model_dir}/*.json").each do |path|
        rows = parse_json_array(path)
        next if rows.empty?

        join_rows = {
          boards_filters: [],
          filters_tags: [],
          assignees_filters: [],
          creators_filters: [],
          closers_filters: []
        }

        mapped_rows = rows.map do |row|
          new_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
          context.id_map[model.name][row["id"]] = new_id

          attrs = import_attributes(row, context, new_id)
          remap_filter_fields!(attrs, context)

          board_ids = Array(row["board_ids"]).filter_map { |id| context.id_map["Board"][id] }
          tag_ids = Array(row["tag_ids"]).filter_map { |id| context.id_map["Tag"][id] }
          assignee_ids = Array(row["assignee_ids"]).filter_map { |id| context.id_map["User"][id] }
          creator_ids = Array(row["creator_ids"]).filter_map { |id| context.id_map["User"][id] }
          closer_ids = Array(row["closer_ids"]).filter_map { |id| context.id_map["User"][id] }

          board_ids.each { |bid| join_rows[:boards_filters] << { board_id: bid, filter_id: new_id } }
          tag_ids.each { |tid| join_rows[:filters_tags] << { filter_id: new_id, tag_id: tid } }
          assignee_ids.each { |uid| join_rows[:assignees_filters] << { assignee_id: uid, filter_id: new_id } }
          creator_ids.each { |uid| join_rows[:creators_filters] << { creator_id: uid, filter_id: new_id } }
          closer_ids.each { |uid| join_rows[:closers_filters] << { closer_id: uid, filter_id: new_id } }

          attrs["params_digest"] = recompute_params_digest(attrs["fields"], board_ids:, tag_ids:, assignee_ids:, creator_ids:, closer_ids:)
          attrs
        end

        ::Filter.insert_all!(mapped_rows)
        insert_join_rows(join_rows)
      end
    end

    def remap_filter_fields!(attrs, context)
      fields = attrs["fields"]
      return unless fields.is_a?(Hash)

      fields = fields.deep_dup
      if fields["card_ids"].is_a?(Array)
        fields["card_ids"] = fields["card_ids"].filter_map { |id| context.id_map["Card"][id] }
      end
      if fields["column_ids"].is_a?(Array)
        fields["column_ids"] = fields["column_ids"].filter_map { |id| context.id_map["Column"][id] }
      end
      attrs["fields"] = fields
    end

    def recompute_params_digest(fields, board_ids:, tag_ids:, assignee_ids:, creator_ids:, closer_ids:)
      fields = fields.is_a?(Hash) ? fields : {}
      params = {
        indexed_by: fields["indexed_by"] || "all",
        sorted_by: fields["sorted_by"] || "latest",
        creation: fields["creation"],
        closure: fields["closure"],
        assignment_status: fields["assignment_status"],
        terms: fields["terms"],
        tag_ids: tag_ids,
        board_ids: board_ids,
        card_ids: fields["card_ids"],
        assignee_ids: assignee_ids,
        creator_ids: creator_ids,
        closer_ids: closer_ids
      }.compact_blank

      ::Filter.digest_params(params)
    end

    def insert_join_rows(join_rows)
      join_rows.each do |table_name, rows|
        next if rows.empty?

        join_model(table_name).insert_all!(rows)
      end
    end

    def join_model(table_name)
      Class.new(ApplicationRecord) do
        self.table_name = table_name.to_s
      end
    end
end
EOF

Specifically: For each `<action-text-attachment>` tag with a `sgid`, I need to extract the `(model_name, old_target_id)` either from the `gid://...` or, and this is important, handle the base64-decoded `_rails.data` for old, signed SGIDs! I *then* replace the `node["sgid"]` with the new SGID. Now, for `ActiveStorage::FileRecordSet`. The `model_dir` is clean. The file uploads are a real area of concern. During *export*, I'm adding each file to the zip. When *importing*, I need to be certain that the file exists in the archive, and then I upload it. class Account::DataTransfer::ActiveStorage::FileRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  LARGE_UPLOAD_THRESHOLD = 100.megabytes

  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: ::ActiveStorage::Blob)
  end

  private
    def model_dir
      "active_storage_files"
    end

    def records
      ::ActiveStorage::Blob.where(account: account).where.not(id: excluded_blob_ids)
    end

    def excluded_blob_ids
      ::ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(account: account, record_type: INTERNAL_RECORD_TYPES).select(:blob_id)
    end

    def export_records
      records.find_each do |blob|
        zip.add_file(file_path(blob.id), compress: false) do |sink|
          blob.download { |chunk| sink.write(chunk) }
        end
      end
    end

    def import_records(context)
      service = ::ActiveStorage::Blob.service

      context.blob_info_map.each do |old_blob_id, info|
        path = file_path(old_blob_id)
        unless zip.exists?(path)
          raise Account::DataTransfer::ImportError, "Missing attachment file in archive: #{info[:filename] || old_blob_id}."
        end

        upload_file(service, path, info, context)
      end
    end

    def file_path(blob_id)
      "#{model_dir}/#{blob_id}"
    end

    def upload_file(service, path, info, context)
      context.uploaded_blob_keys << info[:key]

      if s3_service?(service) && info[:byte_size].to_i >= LARGE_UPLOAD_THRESHOLD
        service.send(:upload_stream,
          key: info[:key],
          content_type: info[:content_type],
          part_size: LARGE_UPLOAD_THRESHOLD
        ) do |sink|
          sink.binmode
          zip.extract(path) { |chunk| sink.write(chunk) }
        end
      else
        tempfile = Tempfile.new([ "import-blob", File.extname(info[:filename].to_s) ])
        tempfile.binmode
        zip.extract(path) { |chunk| tempfile.write(chunk) }
        tempfile.rewind

        service.upload(
          info[:key],
          tempfile,
          checksum: info[:checksum],
          filename: info[:filename],
          content_type: info[:content_type]
        )
      end
    ensure
      tempfile&.close
      tempfile&.unlink
    end

    def s3_service?(service)
      defined?(ActiveStorage::Service::S3Service) && service.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Service::S3Service)
    end
end
EOF

      fragment.css("action-text-attachment").each do |node|
        next if node["sgid"].blank?

        attachable = ::ActionText::Attachable.from_attachable_sgid(node["sgid"])
        if attachable.respond_to?(:to_gid)
          node["sgid"] = attachable.to_gid.to_s

        end

        next
      end

      changed ? fragment.to_html : html
    end

      changed = false

      fragment.css("action-text-attachment").each do |node|
        next if node["sgid"].blank?

        gid = parse_gid(node["sgid"])
        next unless gid

        new_target_id = context.id_map[gid.model_name]&.[](gid.model_id)
        next unless new_target_id

        attachable = find_attachable(gid.model_name, new_target_id)
        next unless attachable

        node["sgid"] = attachable.attachable_sgid
        if attachable.is_a?(::ActiveStorage::Blob) && node["url"].to_s.include?("/rails/active_storage/")
          node["url"] = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.polymorphic_url(
            attachable,
            only_path: true,
            script_name: context.new_account.slug
          )
        end
        changed = true
      end

      changed ? fragment.to_html : html
    end

    def parse_gid(sgid_or_gid)
      if sgid_or_gid.start_with?("gid://")
        GlobalID.parse(sgid_or_gid)
      else
        payload = sgid_or_gid.split("--").first
        data = JSON.parse(Base64.decode64(payload)).dig("_rails", "data")

      nil
    end

      when "ActiveStorage::Blob"
        ::ActiveStorage::Blob.find_by(id: id)
      end
    end

class Account::DataTransfer::Manifest
  attr_reader :account

  def initialize(account = nil)
    @account = account
  end

  def each_record_set
    raise ArgumentError, "No block given" unless block_given?

    record_sets.each do |record_set|
      yield record_set
    end
  end

  def export(zip)
    each_record_set do |record_set|
      record_set.export(zip)
    end
  end

  def import(zip, context)
    each_record_set do |record_set|
      record_set.import(zip, context)
    end

    finalize_import(context)
  end

  private
    def record_sets
      [
        Account::DataTransfer::AccountRecordSet.new(account),
        Account::DataTransfer::UserRecordSet.new(account),
        *record_sets_for(
          ::User::Settings,
          ::Tag,
          ::Board,
          ::Column
        ),
        Account::DataTransfer::EntropyRecordSet.new(account),
        Account::DataTransfer::Board::PublicationRecordSet.new(account),
        *record_sets_for(
          ::Webhook,
          ::Access,
          ::Card,
          ::Comment,
          ::Step,
          ::Assignment,
          ::Tagging,
          ::Closure,
          ::Card::Goldness,
          ::Card::NotNow,
          ::Card::ActivitySpike,
          ::Watch,
          ::Pin,
          ::Reaction,
          ::Mention
        ),
        Account::DataTransfer::FilterRecordSet.new(account),
        record_set_for(::Webhook::DelinquencyTracker),
        Account::DataTransfer::EventRecordSet.new(account),
        *record_sets_for(
          ::Notification,
          ::Notification::Bundle,
          ::Webhook::Delivery
        ),
        Account::DataTransfer::ActiveStorage::BlobRecordSet.new(account),
        record_set_for(::ActiveStorage::VariantRecord),
        Account::DataTransfer::ActionText::RichTextRecordSet.new(account),
        Account::DataTransfer::ActiveStorage::AttachmentRecordSet.new(account),
        Account::DataTransfer::ActiveStorage::FileRecordSet.new(account)
      ]
    end

    def record_sets_for(*models)
      models.map do |model|
        record_set_for(model)
      end
    end

    def record_set_for(model)
      Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet.new(account: account, model: model)
    end

    def finalize_import(context)
      new_account = context.new_account
      new_account.create_join_code! unless new_account.join_code.present?

      if (extra_user_id = context.id_map["__importing_user_created__"]).present?
        board_ids = new_account.boards.all_access.ids
        if board_ids.any?
          now = Time.current
          Access.insert_all!(board_ids.map { |bid|
            { id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, account_id: new_account.id, board_id: bid, user_id: extra_user_id, created_at: now, updated_at: now }
          })
        end
      end

      max_card_number = new_account.cards.maximum(:number) || 0
      if new_account.cards_count < max_card_number
        new_account.update_column(:cards_count, max_card_number)
      end

      reconcile_storage(new_account)
      reindex_search_records(new_account)
    end

    def reconcile_storage(new_account)
      new_account.boards.find_each do |board|
        board.reconcile_storage
        board.materialize_storage
      end
      new_account.reconcile_storage
      new_account.materialize_storage
    end

    def reindex_search_records(new_account)
      new_account.cards.published.includes(:rich_text_description).find_each(batch_size: 100, &:reindex)
      ::Comment.where(account_id: new_account.id)
               .joins(:card).merge(::Card.published)
               .includes(:rich_text_body, :card)
               .find_each(batch_size: 100, &:reindex)
    end
end
EOF

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  include Storage::Totaled

  # Board's own embeds (public_description) count toward itself
  def board_for_storage_tracking
    self
  end

  private
    BATCH_SIZE = 1000

    # Calculate actual storage by summing blob sizes.
    #
    # Storage tracking is a business abstraction - we count what users upload.
    # Original upload bytes only; variants/previews/derivatives excluded.
    # Physical storage optimizations (deduplication, compression) don't affect quotas.
    def calculate_real_storage_bytes
      @card_ids = nil  # Clear memoization for fresh calculation
      card_image_bytes + card_embed_bytes + comment_embed_bytes + board_embed_bytes
    end

    def card_ids
      @card_ids ||= cards.ids
    end

    def card_image_bytes
      sum_blob_bytes_in_batches \
        ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(record_type: "Card", name: "image"),
        card_ids
    end

    def card_embed_bytes
      sum_embed_bytes_for "Card", card_ids
    end

    def comment_embed_bytes
      card_ids.each_slice(BATCH_SIZE).sum do |batch|
        sum_embed_bytes_for "Comment", Comment.where(card_id: batch).ids
      end
    end

    def board_embed_bytes
      sum_embed_bytes_for "Board", [ id ]
    end

    def sum_embed_bytes_for(record_type, record_ids)
      rich_text_ids = ActionText::RichText \
        .where(record_type: record_type, record_id: record_ids).ids

      sum_blob_bytes_in_batches \
        ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(record_type: "ActionText::RichText", name: "embeds"),
        rich_text_ids
    end

    def sum_blob_bytes_in_batches(base_scope, record_ids)
      # Count per-attachment to match ledger model.
      # Same blob attached 3 times = 3x bytes (business abstraction, not physical storage).

        base_scope

      end

    def visible_cards
      user.accessible_cards
          .where("cards.status = ? OR cards.creator_id = ?", "published", user.id)
          .includes(
            :board, :column, :creator, :tags, :steps, :assignees, :closure, :goldness, :not_now,
            { image_attachment: :blob },
            { rich_text_description: { embeds_attachments: :blob } },

          )

    def export_card(zip, card)
      image_metadata = export_card_image(zip, card)
      description_attachments = export_rich_text_attachments(zip, card, card.description)

      comments_json = card.comments.sort_by(&:created_at).map do |comment|

        serialize_comment(comment, comment_attachments)

      zip.add_file("#{card.number}.json", JSON.pretty_generate(payload))

      export_blob(zip, card, card.image.blob)
    end

      return [] unless rich_text&.embeds&.attached?

      rich_text.embeds.map do |embed|
        export_blob(zip, card, embed.blob)
      end
    end

      unless zip.exists?(path)
        zip.add_file(path, compress: false) do |sink|
          blob.download { |chunk| sink.write(chunk) }
        end
      end

      {
        "filename" => blob.filename.to_s,
        "content_type" => blob.content_type,
        "byte_size" => blob.byte_size,
        "path" => path
      }
    end

class Account::Import < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :identity
  belongs_to :account, optional: true

  has_one_attached :file, dependent: :purge_later

  enum :status, %w[ pending processing completed failed ].index_by(&:itself), default: :pending

  validate :file_must_be_attached, on: :create

  def process_later
    Account::ImportJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def process_now
    processing!
    context = Account::DataTransfer::Context.new(importing_identity: identity)

    ApplicationRecord.transaction do
      ZipFile.read_for(file) do |zip|
        Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.new.import(zip, context)
      end
    end

    update!(status: :completed, account: context.new_account, completed_at: Time.current)
    purge_uploaded_file
    AccountMailer.import_completed(self).deliver_now
  rescue ZipFile::Error, Account::DataTransfer::ImportError,
         ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, ActiveStorage::Error => e
    handle_failure(context, e.message)
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.error.report(e, context: { account_import_id: id, identity_id: identity_id })
    handle_failure(context, "An unexpected error occurred while importing your account (#{e.message}).")
  end

  def accessible_to?(user)
    user.present? && user.identity_id == identity_id
  end

  private
    def file_must_be_attached
      errors.add(:file, "must be attached") unless file.attached?
    end

    def handle_failure(context, message)
      context&.cleanup_uploaded_blobs
      update!(status: :failed, account: nil, error_message: message)
      purge_uploaded_file
      AccountMailer.import_failed(self).deliver_now
    end

    def purge_uploaded_file
      file.purge if file.attached?
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.warn("Failed to purge import file for #{id}: #{e.message}")
    end
end
EOF

        format.html { render "exports/expired", status: :gone }
        format.json { head :gone }
      end
    else
      respond_to do |format|
        format.html { render "exports/expired", status: :not_found }
        format.json { head :not_found }
      end
    end
  end
end

It must correctly read entries, support globbing, extract chunks, and have robust safeguards against path traversal vulnerabilities (those `../` attempts are the bane of my existence!). And of course, it *must* raise the appropriate `ZipFile::InvalidError` when fed garbage input. We must ensure the `ZipFile.create_for` and `ZipFile.read_for` methods play nice with local disk attachments, and `ZipFile::RemoteIO` (mocked with WebMock, of course!) reads the size and ranges using HTTP Range requests and functions with the `ZipFile::Reader`.

Next, `test/models/account/export_test.rb`. This is a crucial test of the export process. The goal is to verify that a proper ZIP archive is generated for an account, with *all* relevant tables included. This includes the `accounts`, `users`, `boards`, `columns`, `cards`, and so on. We need to make sure that the `Export` records and blobs are excluded, this is important for performance. Then the test has to send an email with the download link, that the link must work for one day, and expire after that. We must confirm that `Export.cleanup` works as intended, deleting expired exports but keeping active ones safe.

`test/models/user/data_export_test.rb`. This is where the user's data export is tested. It's *critical* that the test exports only the cards the user is allowed to see. This means excluding cards on boards they don't have access to and other users' draft cards. Only published cards on accessible boards and the user's own drafts should be included. We also need to confirm that cards are exported as JSON, complete with comments and all associated media (images and files). Again, a download link must be sent via email, valid for one day and expired after.

Now for the king of tests: `test/models/account/import_test.rb`. This is a *full* round-trip test. We need to make sure that an account can be exported and then successfully imported, including boards (with access restrictions), columns, entropy, cards (including rich text, `@mentions`, and embedded images), comments, reactions, filters, events, webhooks, people, avatars, rich text embeds, and all of the data that goes with all of that. We're importing to a *new* account! We need to test the import under the *same* identity and a *different* one. The main things to verify are that a new account with a new ID and `external_account_id` is created, and that the original account is untouched. The new account should have all the boards, columns, cards, comments, reactions, mentions, filters, etc., and that they all *work*—that the search index works on the imported content, that storage totals are correct, and that a success email is sent with a link to the new account. It is also important that the zip file is cleared up after import. We also need to cover failure scenarios: what happens with corrupt files, missing data, and errors during import? The entire transaction must be atomic. It must roll back completely if anything goes wrong, leaving no trace behind, and the user must get a clear and useful failure message.

Then, controller tests.

-   `test/controllers/account/exports_controller_test.rb`: Verify the admin can initiate and download account exports, and that the export link expires. Verify that regular users don't have access.
-   `test/controllers/users/data_exports_controller_test.rb`: Test user data exports, confirming that only the user can start their own export, not other users' exports.
-   `test/controllers/account/imports_controller_test.rb`: Test all account import controller actions to ensure authentication, file submission, valid and invalid .zip handling, and the atomicity of the import process.

require "test_helper"

class ZipFileTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "writer adds files with content and tracks byte_size and checksum" do
    tempfile = Tempfile.new([ "test", ".zip" ])
    tempfile.binmode

    writer = ZipFile::Writer.new(tempfile)
    writer.add_file("hello.txt", "Hello, World!")
    writer.close

    tempfile.rewind
    actual_bytes = tempfile.read

    assert writer.exists?("hello.txt")
    assert_not writer.exists?("missing.txt")
    assert_equal actual_bytes.bytesize, writer.byte_size
    assert_equal Digest::MD5.base64digest(actual_bytes), writer.checksum
  end

  test "writer adds files with block" do
    tempfile = Tempfile.new([ "test", ".zip" ])
    tempfile.binmode

    writer = ZipFile::Writer.new(tempfile)
    writer.add_file("hello.txt") { |sink| sink.write("Hello, World!") }
    writer.close

    assert writer.exists?("hello.txt")
  end

  test "writer globs entries" do
    tempfile = Tempfile.new([ "test", ".zip" ])
    tempfile.binmode

    writer = ZipFile::Writer.new(tempfile)
    writer.add_file("docs/readme.txt", "Readme")
    writer.add_file("docs/guide.txt", "Guide")
    writer.add_file("images/logo.png", "PNG data")
    writer.close

    assert_equal [ "docs/guide.txt", "docs/readme.txt" ], writer.glob("docs/*.txt")
    assert_equal [ "images/logo.png" ], writer.glob("**/*.png")
  end

  test "reader reads, globs, and extracts files" do
    io = StringIO.new
    writer = ZipFile::Writer.new(io)
    writer.add_file("accounts/000001.json", '[{"name":"Acme"}]')
    writer.add_file("active_storage_files/blob1", "binary-content", compress: false)
    writer.close

    io.rewind
    reader = ZipFile::Reader.new(io)

    assert reader.exists?("accounts/000001.json")
    assert_not reader.exists?("missing.json")
    assert_equal [ "accounts/000001.json" ], reader.glob("accounts/*.json")
    assert_equal '[{"name":"Acme"}]', reader.read("accounts/000001.json")

    extracted = +""
    reader.extract("active_storage_files/blob1") { |chunk| extracted << chunk }
    assert_equal "binary-content", extracted
  end

  test "reader raises InvalidError on corrupt archive" do
    io = StringIO.new("not a zip archive at all")
    reader = ZipFile::Reader.new(io)

    assert_raises ZipFile::InvalidError do
      reader.exists?("anything.json")
    end
  end

  test "remote io reads zip archive via range requests" do
    io = StringIO.new
    writer = ZipFile::Writer.new(io)
    writer.add_file("hello.txt", "Hello from S3!")
    writer.close
    zip_bytes = io.string.b

    url = "https://s3.example.com/bucket/export.zip"
    stub_request(:get, url).to_return do |request|
      range_header = request.headers["Range"]
      if range_header =~ /bytes=(\d+)-(\d+)/
        start_pos = $1.to_i
        end_pos = [ $2.to_i, zip_bytes.bytesize - 1 ].min
        slice = zip_bytes.byteslice(start_pos..end_pos)
        {
          status: 206,
          body: slice,
          headers: {
            "Content-Range" => "bytes #{start_pos}-#{end_pos}/#{zip_bytes.bytesize}",
            "Content-Length" => slice.bytesize.to_s
          }
        }
      else
        { status: 200, body: zip_bytes, headers: { "Content-Length" => zip_bytes.bytesize.to_s } }
      end
    end

    remote_io = ZipFile::RemoteIO.new(url)
    reader = ZipFile::Reader.new(remote_io)

    assert_equal "Hello from S3!", reader.read("hello.txt")
  ensure
    remote_io&.close
  end
end

steps.message: Let's diagnose the `file_attachment` failure and `own_draft` in `rails runner`.
steps.reasoning_content:
**Decoding These Debugging Breadcrumbs**

Okay, let's break this down. First, this "Missing referenced Identity" error is a goldmine. It pinpoints the `Account::ImportTest` failure directly. The traceback leads to `UserRecordSet#import_records`, then to the `remap_foreign_keys!` method, and ultimately to a missing `Identity` within the `context.id_map`. Essentially, it tried to remap an `identity_id` for a `User` that it couldn't find in the context. The fix is to either provide the `row` without the `identity_id` to `super`, or override `remap_foreign_keys!` to avoid remapping that `identity`, since `UserRecordSet` itself handles it with the email address.

Next, this "Failed to save the new associated file_attachment" error in `Export#build_now` is intriguing. It's failing specifically when associating a file with a `card`. The key observation is that this failure ONLY occurs when `card.update!(description: ...)` or `card.image.attach` is called. The error is somewhere in `export.file.attach(...)` which is called in `ZipFile.create_for(file, ...)` during the `generate_export` process. We need to check `attachment.errors` or `blob.errors` with `rails runner` to see *why* the save is failing. The fact that `Account::ExportTest` passes a "expires after 1 day" test, while it fails on the "build_now creates a zip" test is a huge clue. The second test is setting `Current.account`, which is not occurring in the first test. It's likely that the validation is failing because of something that is unique to the current account.

Finally, we have the `User::DataExportTest` failure, specifically the `assert zip.exists?("#{own_draft.number}.json")` assertion. This seems to be a conflict in the generation of the card's `number`. We need to investigate how `own_draft.number` is generated. It looks like the `Card` model has a `before_create :assign_number` which uses `account.increment!(:cards_count)` to generate the number. We need to verify that `own_draft` actually created a card number, and we need to check the fixtures for consistency. The `accounts.yml` file might be misconfigured, leading to a collision, since the `accounts("37s").cards_count` might not match up with `cards.yml` and that is causing a collision.

I'm jumping to `rails runner` to quickly check the errors in #2 and #3. Time to get my hands dirty!

class Account::DataTransfer::UserRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: User)
  end

  private
    def records
      User.where(account: account).includes(:identity)
    end

    def serialize_record(record)
      super.merge("email_address" => record.identity&.email_address)
    end

    def remap_foreign_keys!(attrs, context)
      # UserRecordSet resolves identity_id via email_address, not id_map
    end

    def import_records(context)
      paths = zip.glob("#{model_dir}/*.json")
      raise Account::DataTransfer::ImportError, "This archive does not appear to be a Fizzy account export (missing user data)." if paths.empty?

      seen_identity_ids = Set.new

      paths.each do |path|
        rows = parse_json_array(path)
        next if rows.empty?

        mapped_rows = rows.map do |row|
          new_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
          context.id_map[model.name][row["id"]] = new_id

          identity = find_or_create_identity(row)
          if identity && !seen_identity_ids.add?(identity.id)
            identity = nil
          end

          attrs = import_attributes(row, context, new_id)
          attrs["identity_id"] = identity&.id
          attrs
        end

        User.insert_all!(mapped_rows)
      end

      ensure_importing_identity_has_user(context)
    end

    def find_or_create_identity(row)
      return nil if row["email_address"].blank? || row["active"] == false

      email = row["email_address"].to_s.strip.downcase
      Identity.find_by(email_address: email) || Identity.create!(email_address: email)
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
      Identity.find_by!(email_address: email)
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e
      raise Account::DataTransfer::ImportError, "Invalid user email address #{row["email_address"].inspect}: #{e.message}"
    end

    def ensure_importing_identity_has_user(context)
      identity = context.importing_identity
      return if context.new_account.users.active.exists?(identity_id: identity.id)

      name = identity.users.first&.name || identity.email_address.split("@").first
      user_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate
      now = Time.current
      User.insert_all!([ {
        "id" => user_id,
        "account_id" => context.new_account.id,
        "identity_id" => identity.id,
        "name" => name,
        "role" => "owner",
        "active" => true,
        "verified_at" => now,
        "created_at" => now,
        "updated_at" => now
      } ])
      context.id_map["__importing_user_created__"] = user_id
    end
end
EOF

def perform_enqueued_jobs(...)
  saved_account = Current.account

end

It's designed to ensure jobs don't rely on a leaking `Current.account` from test setup by setting it to nil. And now it clicks! `ActionMailer::TestHelper#assert_emails` calls `perform_enqueued_jobs`!  So, inside `assert_emails 1`, `ZipFile.create_for_disk` is running. steps.message: Let's update `app/models/zip_file.rb` to use `Current.with_account(attachment.record.try(:account))` and re-run the tests.
steps.reasoning_content:
Okay, here's what's going through my mind:

**On the Right Track (Finally!)**

Eureka! I've been staring at this ActiveStorage upload flow and it finally clicked. The `ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!` method, as it stands, is *not* the place to shove in arbitrary model attributes like `:account`. That's a fundamental misunderstanding. The key, the absolutely *perfect* approach, is to use `Current.with_account(attachment.record.try(:account))` to ensure the correct context is set before the blob creation. It's the most robust and correct way to associate the upload with the current account. And the same strategy applies to `create_for_s3`; I should wrap the `create_before_direct_upload!` call inside a `Current.with_account(attachment.record.try(:account))` block. Brilliant!

Now, the next step is crystal clear: I need to go into `app/models/zip_file.rb`, make the necessary code adjustments to leverage this improved understanding, and then run the whole thing again. Time to get this implemented!

arguments.command:
cat <<'EOF' > app/models/zip_file.rb
class ZipFile
  Error = Class.new(StandardError)
  InvalidError = Class.new(Error)

  class << self
    def create_for(attachment, filename:)
      raise ArgumentError, "No block given" unless block_given?

      service = service_for(attachment)

      Current.with_account(attachment.record.try(:account)) do
        if s3_service?(service)
          create_for_s3(attachment, filename: filename, service: service) { |zip| yield zip }
        else
          create_for_disk(attachment, filename: filename) { |zip| yield zip }
        end
      end
    end

    def read_for(attachment)
      raise ArgumentError, "No block given" unless block_given?

      blob = attachment.blob
      service = blob.service

      if s3_service?(service)
        url = service.url(
          blob.key,
          expires_in: 1.day,
          disposition: :attachment,
          filename: blob.filename,
          content_type: blob.content_type
        )
        remote_io = RemoteIO.new(url)
        begin
          yield Reader.new(remote_io)
        ensure
          remote_io.close
        end
      elsif service.respond_to?(:path_for, true)
        path = service.send(:path_for, blob.key)
        raise ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError, "File not found" unless File.exist?(path)

        File.open(path, "rb") do |file|
          yield Reader.new(file)
        end
      else
        blob.open do |tempfile|
          yield Reader.new(tempfile)
        end
      end
    end

    private
      def service_for(attachment)
        reflection = attachment.record.class.reflect_on_attachment(attachment.name)
        service_name = reflection.options[:service_name] || ActiveStorage::Blob.service.name
        ActiveStorage::Blob.services.fetch(service_name)
      end

      def s3_service?(service)
        # The S3 service doesn't get loaded in development unless it's used
        defined?(ActiveStorage::Service::S3Service) && service.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Service::S3Service)
      end

      def create_for_s3(attachment, filename:, service:)
        blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create_before_direct_upload!(
          filename: filename,
          content_type: "application/zip",
          byte_size: 0,
          checksum: "pending"
        )

        writer = Writer.new

        # Use S3's upload_stream directly for write-based streaming.
        # ActiveStorage's upload method expects a read-based IO, but ZipKit
        # needs a write-based stream. The TransferManager's upload_stream
        # yields a writable IO that we can stream directly to.
        service.send(:upload_stream,
          key: blob.key,
          content_type: "application/zip",
          part_size: 100.megabytes
        ) do |write_stream|
          write_stream.binmode
          writer.stream_to(write_stream)
          yield writer
          writer.close
        end

        blob.update!(byte_size: writer.byte_size, checksum: writer.checksum)
        attachment.attach(blob)
      rescue Aws::S3::MultipartUploadError => e
        blob&.destroy
        if e.errors.any?
          raise e.errors.first
        else
          raise e
        end
      rescue
        blob&.destroy
        raise
      end

      def create_for_disk(attachment, filename:)
        tempfile = Tempfile.new([ "export", ".zip" ])
        tempfile.binmode

        writer = Writer.new(tempfile)
        yield writer
        writer.close

        tempfile.rewind
        attachment.attach(io: tempfile, filename: filename, content_type: "application/zip")
      ensure
        tempfile&.close
        tempfile&.unlink
      end
  end
end
EOF

      if comment_ids_with_attachments.any?
        [ self, *comments.where(id: comment_ids_with_attachments).to_a ]
      else
        [ self ]
      end
    end

    def storage_comment_ids_with_attachments
      direct = []
      rich_text_map = {}

      # Stream comment IDs in batches to avoid loading all into memory
      comments.in_batches(of: STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE) do |batch|
        batch_ids = batch.pluck(:id)

        direct.concat \
          ActiveStorage::Attachment
            .where(record_type: "Comment", record_id: batch_ids)
            .distinct
            .pluck(:record_id)

        ActionText::RichText
          .where(record_type: "Comment", record_id: batch_ids)
          .pluck(:id, :record_id)
          .each { |rt_id, comment_id| rich_text_map[rt_id] = comment_id }
      end

      embed_comment_ids = if rich_text_map.any?
        rich_text_map.keys.each_slice(STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE).flat_map do |batch_ids|
          ActiveStorage::Attachment
            .where(record_type: "ActionText::RichText", record_id: batch_ids)
            .distinct
            .pluck(:record_id)
        end.filter_map { |rt_id| rich_text_map[rt_id] }
      else
        []
      end

      (direct + embed_comment_ids).uniq
    end
end
"
}

    assert_equal [ new_jz.id ], new_filter.assignees.ids
    assert_equal [ new_card.id ], new_filter.card_ids

    assert_not_nil assignment_event

  end

    card2 = cards(:layout)
    card2.image.attach(io: File.open(file_fixture("avatar.png")), filename: "avatar.png", content_type: "image/png")

    export = @account.exports.create!(user: @admin)
    export.build_now

    # Remove only the second blob file so the first blob uploads and then the second fails!
    second_blob_id = card2.image.blob.id
    partial_zip = Tempfile.new([ "partial", ".zip" ])

    ZipFile.read_for(export.file) do |reader|

  ensure
    partial_zip&.close
    partial_zip&.unlink
  end
end
